title: Query DB logs for errors/fatals using database scripts (select top 100 + filter) to support troubleshooting
summary: Use database-resident logs and database scripts to retrieve recent log entries limited to “errors and fatals only,” then use the resulting records as evidence for support diagnosis and subsequent troubleshooting/resolution steps.
when_to_use: When you need evidence from database-resident server logs to identify relevant error/fatal patterns for troubleshooting and support handoff.
roles_and_responsibilities: L2_support: Runs the database-resident log query/script approach to retrieve recent “errors and fatals only” entries and provides the resulting records as evidence for diagnosis.
access_or_tools_needed: DB logs in the DB database (as referenced by the source)
Server log view that shows “right click logs” (as referenced by the source)

system_preconditions: Database-resident logs are available in the DB database referenced by the support workflow.

steps.title: Use the database scripts and server log view to inspect DB logs for support
steps.purpose: Establish the correct log source (server “right click logs” backed by DB logs) and the script-based approach for support troubleshooting.
steps.instruction: Using the database scripts referenced by the support workflow, open/locate the server log view described as “right click logs,” where the logs are stored in the DB database.
steps.expected_result: You have access to a server log view backed by DB logs that can be queried/filtered for support troubleshooting.
steps.healthy_condition: The log view you are using is the one described as “right click logs” and is associated with DB logs in the DB database.
steps.failure_condition: You are viewing a log source that is not the server “right click logs” view or is not tied to the DB database logs.

actions.label: Open server log view (right click logs) tied to DB logs
actions.exact_action: Use the “right click logs” on the server, where the logs are in the DB logs in the DB database we have.

steps.title: Limit results to recent entries using a “select top 100” query pattern
steps.purpose: Reduce the query scope to recent log entries to make troubleshooting evidence manageable and relevant.
steps.instruction: Run the database query pattern described as “select top 100 and filter if I want something” to limit results to recent entries.
steps.expected_result: A result set/list of log records is returned with a “top 100” style limit (recent entries).
steps.healthy_condition: The query returns a bounded list of recent records (top 100) rather than an unbounded/full log history.
steps.failure_condition: The query returns too many records (not limited to a “top 100” style subset) or does not return a recent-entry list.

actions.label: Run “select top 100” query pattern
actions.exact_action: “I mean I just select top 100 and filter if I want something.”

steps.title: Apply filtering to narrow results to relevant entries
steps.purpose: Narrow the recent log results to the relevant subset needed for diagnosis.
steps.instruction: Apply the described filter step (“filter if I want something”) to narrow the “top 100” results to the relevant entries you are investigating.
steps.expected_result: The result set is narrowed to only the entries matching your chosen filter criteria.
steps.healthy_condition: The filtered result set contains fewer, more relevant log records than the initial “top 100” list.
steps.failure_condition: Filtering is not applied (results remain unfiltered) or filtering produces an empty/irrelevant set when you expect matches.

steps.title: Confirm the log view is restricted to “errors and fatals only”
steps.purpose: Ensure the evidence set contains only the intended severity levels for the troubleshooting workflow.
steps.instruction: Verify that the log output you are using is restricted to “errors and fatals only,” consistent with the described server log view behavior.
steps.expected_result: The displayed/returned log records are limited to errors and fatals only.
steps.healthy_condition: No non-error/non-fatal log activity appears in the result set you are using for diagnosis.
steps.failure_condition: The log output includes broader log activity beyond “errors and fatals only.”

actions.label: Verify severity restriction
actions.exact_action: Confirm “Those are like right? Those are errors and fatals only.”

stop_or_escalate_if: If the logs are not restricted to errors/fatals, adjust the query/filter so only errors and fatals are shown.

steps.title: Use the resulting error/fatal records as evidence for diagnosis and next steps
steps.purpose: Convert the retrieved error/fatal records into actionable evidence for support diagnosis and resolution steps.
steps.instruction: Use the filtered error/fatal records returned from the DB logs as the evidence set to match against the expected error type/patterns and to support subsequent diagnosis and resolution steps.
steps.expected_result: You have a filtered list of recent error/fatal log entries that can be used as evidence for the troubleshooting workflow.
steps.healthy_condition: The evidence set consists of recent entries limited to errors/fatals and is suitable for identifying the relevant expected error type/pattern.
steps.failure_condition: No relevant error/fatal records appear for the issue you are investigating.

actions.label: Collect evidence from filtered records
actions.exact_action: Use the “errors and fatals only” DB log records as evidence for support diagnosis and resolution steps.

stop_or_escalate_if: If no relevant error/fatal records appear, stop and escalate to the support handoff/RCA process described in the source.

success_criteria: A filtered list of recent DB log entries is produced that is restricted to “errors and fatals only.”
The resulting records are usable as evidence for matching an expected error type/pattern and supporting subsequent diagnosis/resolution steps.
healthy_conditions: The log output used for troubleshooting contains only errors and fatals (not all log activity).
The query is limited to recent entries (described as “select top 100”).
failure_conditions: The log output includes non-error/non-fatal activity (not restricted to “errors and fatals only”).
No relevant error/fatal records appear for the investigation, requiring escalation.
escalation_guidance: If no relevant error/fatal records appear, stop and escalate to the support handoff/RCA process described in the source.
missing_details: The packet does not provide explicit DB name, table name, or exact SQL/script text beyond the pattern “select top 100 and filter.”
The packet does not provide the exact UI steps/controls for the “right click logs” server view (only that it exists and is used).
The packet does not specify the exact filter criteria/fields used to narrow results beyond the general “filter if I want something” guidance.
